title: Energy, work and power
overview: Calculate work done, kinetic/gravitational potential energy, and power in mechanical systems. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Calculate work by a constant force at an angle to displacement.
Use kinetic and gravitational potential energy.
Apply work–energy and conservation of energy.
Use average and instantaneous power, including P=Fv.

definitions.definition: Energy transferred when a force acts through a displacement.
Energy associated with height, mgh relative to a chosen datum.
Rate of doing work or transferring energy.
A force opposing motion and dissipating mechanical energy.

sections.title: Work by a force
content: For constant force F and displacement d with angle θ between them, work is Fd cosθ. Work is positive when the force helps motion, negative when it opposes, and zero when perpendicular.
bullets: Use the angle between force and displacement, not automatically the slope angle.

sections.title: Energy stores
content: Kinetic energy is ½mv² and gravitational potential change is mgΔh. Only height change matters for GPE, even on a curved path. Choose a convenient zero level and use energy differences consistently.
bullets: Mass cancels in some smooth gravity problems but not all.

sections.title: Work–energy principle
content: Change in KE equals total work done by external forces. Equivalently, initial KE+GPE+work supplied equals final KE+GPE+energy dissipated. Include resistance as negative work or a positive loss, but not both.
bullets: Energy methods avoid time and often avoid resolving acceleration along a changing path.
Mechanical energy is conserved only when no non-conservative work is done.

sections.title: Power
content: Average power=work/time. Instantaneous power for a force parallel to motion is P=Fv. For a vehicle climbing at constant speed, driving power balances the rate of gain of GPE plus work against resistance.
bullets: If acceleration is present, include ma in the force balance before using P=Fv.

formulas.label: Instantaneous power
formulas.note: For the force component along the velocity.

diagram.title: Energy, work and power: revision route

examTips: Write an energy ledger with initial, final, supplied and dissipated terms.
Keep signs consistent—do not count resistance twice.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Using path length instead of vertical height in mgh.
Using P=Fv with the total force when only one force's power is required.
Conserving mechanical energy despite friction without including its work.

quickRecall.question: When is work by a force zero?
quickRecall.answer: When the force is perpendicular to the displacement.

quickRecall.question: What does change in kinetic energy equal?
quickRecall.answer: The total work done by external forces.

quickRecall.question: Why does a curved smooth track still use mgh?
quickRecall.answer: Gravitational potential energy depends only on vertical height change.

quickRecall.question: When may P=Fv be used directly?
quickRecall.answer: For the force component acting in the direction of instantaneous motion.
